job.title: Senior Mechanical Project Engineer
job.description:
RobLawMax Recruitment has been appointed exclusively to recruit a Senior Mechanical Project Engineer for an established Canterbury mechanical engineering business.

The company provides end-to-end engineering services across the dairy, food processing, energy and wider industrial sectors. Its work spans process and thermal plant, boilers and pressure equipment, piping systems, material handling equipment, structural steelwork and complex mechanical upgrades.

Early contractor involvement is underway on a major industrial design-and-build project. High-level design and pricing have commenced, with detailed design, procurement and delivery expected to follow later this year. The initial programme will run through to 2028, with further opportunities expected to provide an ongoing pipeline of complex industrial work.

The business is now seeking an experienced mechanical Project Engineer who can take a leading role in the delivery of this programme.

The role

This is a broad project leadership position combining engineering, commercial and delivery responsibility.

Working alongside an established engineering, project and workshop team, you will help drive the project from early design through procurement, fabrication, installation and commissioning.

You will:

  • Take ownership of engineering and project delivery across a major industrial design-and-build project
  • Establish and manage project programmes, budgets, deliverables and reporting requirements
  • Coordinate mechanical design and technical inputs across internal engineers, clients, suppliers and specialist consultants
  • Manage project scope, programme, cost, risk, quality and commercial performance
  • Act as a key interface with the client and maintain alignment across project stakeholders
  • Review concepts, calculations, 3D models, drawings, specifications and technical documentation
  • Ensure engineering solutions are safe, practical, buildable and aligned with project requirements
  • Prepare and manage procurement packages, supplier specifications and subcontracted scopes of work
  • Coordinate equipment selection, procurement and long-lead items
  • Work closely with fabrication, construction and site teams
  • Manage technical queries, design changes and project variations
  • Support installation, testing, commissioning and final handover
  • Contribute to the development of project systems, engineering processes and internal capability

While this is primarily a project leadership role, you will need strong mechanical design understanding and the ability to remain technically involved when required. You won’t necessarily produce every model or drawing yourself, but you must be able to guide, challenge and review the engineering work being delivered.

About you

You will be a practical mechanical engineer with experience delivering industrial, manufacturing, energy or infrastructure projects through multiple stages of the project lifecycle.

You may already be operating as a Senior Project Engineer, or you could be an accomplished Design / Project Engineer who is ready to take greater ownership of larger and more complex projects.

Ideally, you will bring:

  • A mechanical engineering degree or equivalent tertiary qualification
  • Strong mechanical project engineering and design experience
  • Experience delivering projects through design, procurement, fabrication, installation and commissioning
  • The ability to manage programme, budget, risk, quality and stakeholder requirements
  • Strong client-facing communication and commercial awareness
  • Experience coordinating multidisciplinary engineers, suppliers and subcontractors
  • Sound mechanical design judgement and a practical understanding of fabrication and construction
  • The ability to review 3D models, engineering drawings and technical documentation
  • Experience with SolidWorks or another parametric 3D modelling package
  • A collaborative, accountable and delivery-focused approach

Experience leading major projects would be valuable, but it is not the only pathway into the role. The company is also interested in high-performing engineers who have successfully led smaller projects or substantial work packages and are ready to step into broader project responsibility.

Experience involving process plant, boilers, pressure equipment, piping, heat-transfer systems, material handling equipment or other heavy industrial plant would be advantageous. However, candidates from other mechanical design-and-build, manufacturing, energy and project-based environments are encouraged to apply.

The opportunity

This is a permanent, full-time position based in Christchurch.

It offers the opportunity to take a leading role in a substantial industrial programme from its earliest design stages and remain involved through procurement, fabrication, installation and commissioning.

You will join an experienced and supportive engineering team, work closely with in-house fabrication capability and help build project knowledge and systems that will support the business well beyond the initial programme.

For an established Senior Project Engineer, this is an opportunity to lead a major project without moving away from the practical and technical side of engineering. For a strong Design / Project Engineer ready for the next step, it offers genuine scope to grow into significant project leadership with the support of an experienced team.

For a confidential discussion, contact Peter Henderson on 027 441 9300 at RobLawMax Recruitment, or apply online with your CV.

job.title: Senior Power Electronics Engineer
job.description:
Kea Aerospace has partnered with RobLawMax Recruitment to appoint a Senior Power Electronics Engineer to its Christchurch-based team.

Kea is developing the Kea Atmos, a solar-powered, remotely piloted stratospheric aircraft designed to remain airborne continuously for months at a time. Operating approximately 20 kilometres above the Earth, it will support maritime surveillance, environmental monitoring, disaster management and other applications.

The Kea Atmos will be the largest unmanned aircraft built in the Southern Hemisphere. This newly created role offers the opportunity to own critical aircraft electronics and see your designs progress from initial concept through to flight.

The opportunity

You will take ownership of electronics development from establishing requirements and system architecture through to detailed design, board bring-up, verification and flight-test support.

Rather than receiving a fully developed specification, you will work with the wider aircraft team to determine what is needed, make sound technical trade-offs and deliver robust, working hardware.

Depending on your particular area of expertise, your responsibilities will include:

  • Defining electronic system requirements, architecture and technical trade studies.
  • Leading the design and optimisation of power-conversion, distribution, monitoring and data-collection electronics.
  • Designing analogue circuits, schematics, magnetic components and PCB layouts.
  • Developing high-efficiency, lightweight electronic solutions suitable for an aircraft with limited available energy.
  • Modelling efficiency, mass, cost and performance to guide design decisions.
  • Building, testing and debugging prototypes, including investigating unexpected faults and unusual operating conditions.
  • Addressing EMI/EMC, thermal performance, packaging, reliability and manufacturability.
  • Supporting environmental qualification, aircraft integration and flight testing.
  • Producing clear technical reports that explain findings and inform design decisions.
  • Collaborating with design, test and manufacturing colleagues to deliver flight-ready hardware.

About you

We are looking for a Senior Electronics Engineer with at least seven years’ hands-on experience and deep expertise in power electronics or a closely related electronics field.

Power electronics is the preferred background. However, Kea is also open to experienced engineers from other domains, such as embedded hardware, where the overall technical fit is strong.

You must be a confident communicator with strong spoken and written English. In particular, you will need to produce high-quality technical reports that clearly explain your findings and inform design choices.

Depending on your background, your experience is likely to include several of the following:

  • DC-DC switch-mode power supplies, converter topology selection and analogue control.
  • Analogue circuit design, electromagnetics, magnetic-component design or discrete logic.
  • Embedded hardware and complex PCB design.
  • Defining system requirements rather than relying on an existing specification.
  • System-level power architecture, budgeting and technical trade studies.
  • Designing, building, testing and fault-finding printed circuit boards.
  • Modelling, simulation, validation and structured system verification.
  • Schematic-capture and PCB-layout software. Kea uses Altium, although experience with comparable packages is transferable.
  • Understanding how PCB layout affects EMI/EMC, thermal performance and manufacturability.
  • Taking electronic hardware from initial concept through to a tested working product.

You will also need to be comfortable working autonomously within a small, agile engineering team where no one will necessarily tell you exactly what needs to be built or how to build it.

Relevant backgrounds

Aerospace or spacecraft experience would be advantageous but is not essential. Relevant experience may come from electric vehicles, battery systems, electric propulsion, aviation, defence, drones or other high-reliability and harsh-environment electronic systems.

The key is your ability to apply strong fundamental knowledge to the unusual conditions encountered at stratospheric altitude, including extreme cold, very thin air and an increased risk of electrical arcing.

Additional experience

Experience in any of the following would be useful but is not essential:

  • Lithium-ion battery systems or solar-array integration
  • Aerospace EMI/EMC standards and FMEA/FMECA
  • Environmental or qualification testing
  • Taking designs from prototype into production
  • Design for Manufacturability and Design for Testability
  • High-speed digital interfaces and structured engineering-change processes
  • Python or another high-level language for modelling, automation or testing
  • Mentoring engineers and contributing to wider technical development

Why Kea Aerospace?

  • Own critical aircraft electronics rather than one small part of an established product.
  • Work on technology unlike anything else being developed in this part of the world.
  • See your designs move rapidly from concept and bench testing to integration and flight.
  • Join a talented, mission-driven team where your decisions directly shape the aircraft.

Kea is interested in both New Zealand-based and international candidates. Applications should clearly state your current New Zealand work status or whether immigration support would be required.

For security and safety reasons, police vetting will be undertaken before an offer of employment is made.

For a confidential discussion, contact Peter Henderson on 027 441 9300 at RobLawMax Recruitment, or apply with your CV and a brief summary of electronic hardware you have personally taken from design through to testing.

job.title: Senior Thermal Systems Analyst
job.description:
RobLawMax Recruitment is partnering exclusively with Kea Aerospace on this appointment

Help solve the thermal challenges of a solar-powered aircraft designed for long-duration operation in the stratosphere.

Kea Aerospace is developing the Kea Atmos - a solar-powered, remotely piloted stratospheric aircraft designed to fly continuously for extended periods at approximately 20km altitude, delivering aerial intelligence for applications including maritime surveillance, environmental monitoring and disaster management.

As development of the Kea Atmos progresses, Kea is looking for an experienced Senior Thermal Systems Engineer to lead thermal design, analysis, testing and optimisation across the aircraft.

Operating in the stratosphere presents a particularly challenging thermal environment. Extremely low ambient temperatures are combined with very low atmospheric density, limiting conventional heat rejection while different aircraft systems operate across very different thermal conditions.

This is an opportunity for an experienced thermal engineer to apply strong first-principles knowledge and modelling capability to a genuinely unusual engineering problem, and to see that work progress from analysis and design through physical testing and ultimately integration onto the aircraft.

The Role

Working as part of Kea's multidisciplinary engineering team in Christchurch, you will take a leading role in developing and optimising thermal management solutions for the Kea Atmos.

An initial area of focus will be the thermal performance of the aircraft's powertrain and associated systems, working closely with battery, avionics and other engineering disciplines.

You will:

  • Lead thermal design, analysis, testing and optimisation across aircraft systems.
  • Apply first-principles analysis, hand calculations and numerical modelling to understand and predict thermal behaviour.
  • Develop reduced-order and 1D thermal models, including developing your own modelling tools and scripts.
  • Use 3D CFD and multiphysics simulation where appropriate to investigate more complex thermal behaviour and de-risk designs prior to hardware build.
  • Develop lightweight and energy-efficient thermal solutions while considering Size, Weight and Power (SWaP) trade-offs.
  • Work with physical hardware through prototyping, testing and validation, correlating test results against analytical and numerical models.
  • Work closely with mechanical, electrical, battery, avionics and other engineering disciplines to optimise system-level performance.
  • Communicate analysis, findings and recommendations through clear technical reporting that supports engineering design decisions.
  • Contribute across the full engineering lifecycle from concept and analysis through to testing, integration and flight hardware.

What We're Looking For

The core requirements for this appointment are:

  • 8+ years of dedicated thermal engineering experience, with thermal design and/or analysis forming a significant part of your engineering career.
  • Strong understanding of heat transfer and thermal fundamentals, with demonstrated capability in first-principles calculations and/or 1D thermal simulation and/or 3D CFD.
  • Genuine programming capability, ideally using Python, although experience with MATLAB, C/C++ or other relevant engineering programming languages will also be considered.
  • The ability to develop, understand and interrogate your own engineering models rather than relying solely on commercial simulation packages.
  • Strong English communication and technical writing capability, including experience producing quality technical reports that inform engineering and design decisions.
  • A relevant Engineering degree or equivalent experience.

Practical experience applying thermal analysis to physical hardware, including testing and validation, will be highly regarded.

Your Background

Previous aerospace experience is not essential.

Kea is interested first and foremost in finding an engineer with genuine depth in thermal engineering, strong fundamentals and the ability to apply those skills to real-world engineering problems.

Relevant experience could therefore have been developed within aerospace or space systems, but equally within areas such as:

  • Automotive, EV or motorsport
  • Battery, powertrain or electronics thermal management
  • Defence and advanced technology
  • Nuclear, energy or power generation
  • Medical or scientific equipment
  • Advanced product development and other high-performance engineering environments

Experience with high-altitude, low-pressure, space or other extreme environments would be advantageous.

Additional breadth across areas such as multiphysics analysis, FEA, structural dynamics, aerodynamics, electrical systems, mechanical design, CAD, materials, manufacturing and DFM would also be valuable within Kea's multidisciplinary engineering environment.

Why Kea Aerospace?

Kea offers the opportunity to work on a highly unusual engineering programme and to have genuine involvement across the full development lifecycle.

The Kea Atmos is designed, developed, tested and built in Christchurch, allowing engineers to remain close to the physical product and see their work progress from modelling and analysis through to hardware, testing, integration and flight.

As part of a growing and multidisciplinary team, there is also scope to contribute beyond a narrowly defined technical discipline and help shape engineering solutions as the aircraft continues to develop.

Kea offers an employee share option plan, flexible working hours, and a working environment focused on combining ambitious engineering with a sustainable work/life balance. You’ll be based in Kea’s newly opened Christchurch engineering and manufacturing facility, providing a modern environment in which to design, build and test the aircraft.

Location

Given the specialist nature of the appointment, applications are welcomed from experienced thermal engineers based elsewhere in New Zealand or internationally who would consider relocating to Christchurch.

Relocation support may be considered on a case-by-case basis.
